questions_and_answers.answer: The coach should prioritise water, relaxation, shade, and progressive acclimatisation during outdoor football practises in hot and humid conditions to prevent heat-related diseases . Heat exhaustion and heatstroke can occur in football players who practise outdoors in hot and humid weather. The coach should take the following actions to protect players from heat-related illnesses: Hydration: Remind participants to drink water before, during, and after practise. In hot conditions, hydration replaces sweated fluids. Breaks & rest: Allow players to relax and cool down throughout practise. If possible, don't practise in the heat. Shade and Cooling Stations: Provide shaded places or cooling stations for players to rest between workouts. Lightweight clothes: Players should wear lightweight, loose-fitting, and breathable clothes for enhanced air circulation and cooling.
